title: World Cinema Radar — the podcast, Thursday 29 October 2026

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Hello, and welcome to World Cinema Radar, the podcast. It's Thursday the twenty-ninth of October, and I'm {A}.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And I'm {B}. <chuckle> Good morning, {A}. Quick warning: today's edition is a short one.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It is. We looked hard this morning, and honestly? There wasn't much we could verify properly. So we chose fewer stories over shaky ones.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which I respect. Better a small radar that works than a big one that makes things up.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So here's the plan. First, what HBO Max is doing in Spain in November. A lot of films, and a couple of very good ones.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then some theatre news from the National Theatre at Home, with Tom Stoppard in the mix.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And then Seminci in Valladolid, which closes this Saturday with a film by Gael García Bernal.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: After that, the calendar, and our picks. Everything comes from today's edition, with every source in the app. No spoilers, as always.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. Shall we start with the streaming news?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let's go.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, HBO Max in Spain. Their November calendar is out, and the interesting part is the films. On the fifth of November, three titles land on the same day.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Jojo Rabbit, The Whale and Black Swan. <short pause> That's quite a Thursday evening.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It is! Jojo Rabbit is Taika Waititi's satire, Black Swan is Darren Aronofsky's psychological horror, and The Whale is the third one.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I love that Black Swan is in there. Ballet, paranoia, a mirror that never quite behaves. <chuckle> It's horror dressed up as a drama, or the other way round.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Exactly. And I'd say Jojo Rabbit is the perfect companion piece, if you like period settings with a sharp edge.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Hm. |oh, that's a strange double bill| But it works. One is all nerves, the other is all irony.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Then there's a second wave on the twelfth. Dangerous Minds, Contact and Little Miss Sunshine. And on the twenty-sixth, two more, Locura padre and El soldado de Dios.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Now, one thing we should say clearly. These are dates for Spain, and they come from specialist press, not from HBO itself. So double-check on the platform.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. And the articles we read don't give years or directors for every title, so we're not going to pretend they do.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Fair. What about the Spanish side?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One more thought on the films. When a platform drops three big titles on one day, it is usually building a kind of mini season. Not a festival, but an evening menu.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A menu! <chuckle> Okay, so what would you order?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Black Swan first, because it is tense and it is short enough for a weeknight. Then Jojo Rabbit on the weekend, when you want something with more air in it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And The Whale for a night when you are in the mood to be a bit sad. I'm only guessing from the title and the date, mind you. The article doesn't tell us more.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right, and that is the point. We are reporting a calendar, not a review. If we cite a critic, we will say who.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good rule. Also, I like that the list mixes very old favourites with brand new Spanish releases. It's a catalogue that wants to be everything for everybody.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Which is fine. For us, the question is simply what fits the profile. Horror, history, clever comedies, international cinema. And this month, honestly, it's a modest yes.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A modest yes. <short pause> I'll take it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: There's Tres de más, a Spanish comedy, coming on the twentieth after its run in cinemas. That one is for people who want something lighter.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the series?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: One question, {A}. If someone only has time for one title from this list, which one?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Black Swan. It is the one that fits the profile best. Psychological horror, an artist under pressure, and a director with a very precise eye.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I would maybe say Jojo Rabbit, because the period setting is such a strong thing for me. But I see your point.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: See? Two different answers, same calendar. <chuckle> That is what a good list does.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the nice thing is that all of it is on one platform. No hunting around.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: True. Although, it is a platform, so the usual rule applies. Things come and go. Watch what you like while it is there.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Wise words. Moving on, then?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Moving on.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The Gilded Age is back for season four on the second of November. Then an Italian series, Melania Rea, on the sixth. And Ciudad de Dios, the new batch of six episodes, on the eighth.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And Infamia on the thirteenth, the thriller we mentioned earlier this week. The same day, two European productions appear in the lists, one Polish called Silent Night and one Hungarian called Maniacs of Truth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Which I'm curious about, but we know nothing else yet. That's all the articles say.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So, the verdict? Is this a big month for our profile?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Medium. Three out of five on our scale, with medium confidence. It's not a news breakthrough, it's a good reason to have Black Swan on your list.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And that's an editorial score, remember. Not a critics' score.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And a reminder for anyone outside Spain. Everything here is about the Spanish catalogue. Other countries will get different lists.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Always worth saying. The same film can be on a platform in one country and gone in the next.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Now, theatre. National Theatre at Home has posted its coming-soon page, and there are two classics we like.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Arcadia first. Tom Stoppard's play, directed by Carrie Cracknell and produced by the Old Vic. It arrives on the twenty-sixth of November.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oh, Arcadia. <breath> It's the one with the two time periods in the same room, isn't it? I remember it being clever and, weirdly, moving.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's it. Ideas, wit, a country house, and a lot of people being wrong in interesting ways.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Honestly, that's my favourite kind of play. |ha, mine too|

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Then on the first of December, The Playboy of the Western World, by John Millington Synge. Directed by Caitríona McLaughlin, with Nicola Coughlan, Éanna Hardwicke and Siobhán McSweeney.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A comic tragedy about a big story told in a small pub. And Nicola Coughlan in it, which is lovely.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: There are others, too. Kinky Boots on the first of December, A Child's Christmas in Wales on the eighth, and Owain and Henry next March.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And this week's one, Les Liaisons Dangereuses, goes live on the third of November. We talked about it on Monday.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. Now here's the careful part. The page says you can subscribe monthly or yearly, or rent, and there's a one-week free trial. But it doesn't say which plays are on which model.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And it doesn't give the year of the recording or the subtitles.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: No. So this isn't a full recommendation card. It's a calendar notice, and we say so.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: What I like about this kind of service is that you can see a play you will never get to see in London. The theatre travels to your living room.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, though it's different from the cinema. A filmed play is a record of a night, with cameras placed by someone else. It can be wonderful, or a bit flat.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's why we are careful. Until we know the year of the recording and the cast, we don't promise anything.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And for Arcadia, the page doesn't list a cast at all. So we can only say who directed it and where it was produced.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Which is the Old Vic, with Carrie Cracknell. That much we do know.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So if you are a Stoppard person, the twenty-sixth of November goes in the diary. If you are a Synge person, the first of December.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And if you are a Kinky Boots person, also the first of December. <giggle> Busy day for the National Theatre.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A very busy day. Honestly, I would love to see the first of December as a double bill, a comic tragedy and a musical. Strange, but fun.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Still, Arcadia gets a four out of five from us, with medium confidence. We haven't seen the recording yet.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I should also say something about the free trial. A week of unlimited access is a good way to try a service without a long commitment.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It is, and the page says so. But we don't know the prices, because the page doesn't list them. So we won't quote any.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. No numbers we can't check.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And if you rent single plays instead, it depends on the title. Again, the page doesn't say which ones.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So the advice is simple. Check the page when the date arrives, and decide then.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Which, for Arcadia, is the twenty-sixth of November. About four weeks from now.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Seminci, the Valladolid festival. It closes this Saturday, the thirty-first, with a film called Hombre al agua.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's Gael García Bernal's third film as a director. He also wrote it, and he stars in it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: He plays Camilo, a Cuban lifeguard who saves a Mexican businessman. And that's as far as we'll go, because spoilers.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: <chuckle> A lifeguard story with no spoilers. We can do that.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The cast also includes Esmeralda Pimentel, Débora Nascimento, Natalia Oreiro and Ricky Martin. It's described as a comedy about class and masculinity.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the festival says this will be his first visit to Valladolid, even though two films he was part of played there before. Museo in 2018 and Magallanes last year.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The festival opened with Lili Horvát's My Notes on Mars, which is in competition, with Mackenzie Davis and Rupert Friend.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Now, the important bit. The competition results, the Espiga de Oro, are due on Saturday too.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. And a caveat. The press release we read is dated the fifth of October. It doesn't give a time for the closing, and it doesn't say when the film opens in Spanish cinemas.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And we haven't seen it. So it gets three out of five from us, with low confidence. A social comedy, so a bit outside the usual horror and history territory.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I find it interesting that a festival picks a comedy to close. Usually the last night is the glamorous one, the prize night.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And this year the prizes and the closing film arrive together on the same Saturday. It makes the day feel like a little finale.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Do we know who is in the jury, or the favourites? Because I'm curious.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Not from the sources we have today. So we won't guess. What we know is that the festival ran from the twenty-third to the thirty-first of October.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Fair enough. Another thing I noticed: García Bernal has a history with Seminci films, even as an actor, without having come in person.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That is what the release says. His first visit, after Museo and Magallanes. It is a sweet detail for a festival that likes its history.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And a nice reminder that Valladolid is one of the places in Spain that takes international cinema seriously.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Agreed. If you can't go, keep an eye on the news on Saturday evening. We will bring the results when they are official.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One more small thing. The release talks about Lili Horvát having won the Espiga de Oro at the sixty-fifth edition. So she is a returning guest, not a newcomer.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oh, that's a nice detail. She won before, she opened this year, and she is in competition again.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. A festival that likes to bring its friends back.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which is a good way to build a family of filmmakers. And a good reason to follow Valladolid from afar.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: But a closing night with a comedy is a nice choice. It's gentle after nine days of heavy drama.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right, the calendar. Saturday the thirty-first, in Spain: Seminci closes with Hombre al agua, and the results come out.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Monday the second of November, HBO Max Spain: season four of The Gilded Age.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Tuesday the third: Les Liaisons Dangereuses on National Theatre at Home.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thursday the fifth, HBO Max Spain: Jojo Rabbit, The Whale and Black Swan.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The thirteenth, HBO Max Spain: Infamia. The twentieth: Tres de más.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And in the theatre column, Arcadia on the twenty-sixth, then The Playboy of the Western World and Kinky Boots on the first of December.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Platform dates can change, so check with the service.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: If you want one tip, it's this. The first week of November is the busy one. The Gilded Age on the second, the National Theatre play on the third, three films on the fifth.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So that is one week, with a bit of everything. A series, a stage recording, and a cinema evening.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And after that it is calmer, until the end of the month. So plan accordingly.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Exactly. Plan accordingly, and keep a seat free for Saturday's festival news.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Before we leave the calendar, a note on honesty. These dates are the ones we found in today's sources. If a date isn't here, it doesn't mean nothing happens.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Exactly. It only means we haven't verified it. Last week's editions have other dates, and you can find them in the app's archive.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Our picks, then. Number one, Black Swan, on HBO Max Spain on the fifth of November. Four out of five, high confidence for the genre.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I'd say that's the safe choice, but a good one. You've probably seen it, but it deserves a rewatch.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Number two, Arcadia, from the twenty-sixth, on National Theatre at Home. Four out of five, medium confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And number three, Hombre al agua on Saturday at Seminci. Three out of five, low confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: One thing about these picks. They are not a guarantee of quality. They are a match between what is coming and what we like.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. The scores are editorial affinity, from nought to five. Not what critics say, and not what the public says.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And if you only watch one of the three, make it the one you can see at home on a rainy evening.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Black Swan, then. <laugh> Lights off, volume up, and a very good chair.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And we tell you how confident we are, because we haven't seen everything. We would rather admit it than pretend.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That is the idea of the Radar. Careful, curious, and honest about the gaps.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A modest list today, but honest.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So, the idea of the day: a quiet news day is still a good day to plan your November.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thank you for listening, and for putting up with a small edition today.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Small but true. Tomorrow we will look for more. And in the meantime, go and watch something good.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Put Black Swan and Arcadia in your diary, and keep an eye on Valladolid on Saturday. See you tomorrow on the Radar.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: See you tomorrow. <laugh> Bring a bigger edition.
